sources.entry: CC Harness by lookfree - Desktop workbench that reads Claude Code session files locally and renders the subagent and workflow topology as a live graph, with per-node latency, token cost, and nesting depth. Token spend is broken down by source (base session, skills, subagents, MCP) and can be traced from a cost bucket to the exact message that produced it.

summary.one_liner: CC Harness is an open-source Electron desktop workbench that reads your local Claude Code session and config files (~/.claude) to visualize subagent topology, token costs, hooks, skills, loops, and memory.
keywords: see what claude code is doing
summary.what_it_does: CC Harness reads Claude Code session jsonl files and renders the subagent and workflow call tree as a live graph, showing per-node latency, token cost, and nesting depth. A per-session token cost panel splits spend across base session, skills, subagents, MCP, and plugins, and clicking a bucket lets you jump to the specific message that produced the cost. It includes a repricing optimizer that estimates savings from running current Opus tokens at Sonnet rates. A hook sandbox dry-runs hooks with simulated input and reports stdout, stderr, exit code, and transformed result in an isolated environment. Other panels aggregate ScheduleWakeup loops, analyze skill trigger keywords with a Mermaid diagram, map dependencies between skills, hooks, commands and MCP servers, and snapshot MEMORY.md diffs around dream passes. It also shows a config layer map of skills, commands, agents and hooks across user, project and plugin sources.
use_cases: debug a stuck Claude Code subagent workflow
see where Claude Code token spend is going
dry-run a Claude Code hook before using it
find which skills or MCP servers cost the most
hand off a Claude Code project config to a teammate
monitor scheduled loops and background tasks
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (not given in README)
npm run electron:dev  (desktop mode, full features)
notable: Traces a token cost bucket back to the exact message in the session replay
Hook sandbox runs with only PATH, HOME and TMPDIR set, with no API tokens or credentials passed in
Repricing optimizer computes dollar savings from real session data for Opus-to-Sonnet swaps
Dependency graph assembles related nodes into numbered workflow chains
Read-only with respect to conversations; it does not act as a chat client or CLI replacement
caveats: Desktop builds are unsigned, so macOS needs xattr or right-click Open and Windows needs SmartScreen bypass on first launch
Web mode is read-only; live monitoring, hook sandbox execution, MCP tests and file watching require desktop mode
Requires Node.js 18+ and an installed Claude Code CLI with ~/.claude present
Phase 3 features (workflow templates, harness benchmark, onboarding tour) are listed as planned, not done
